classification.difficultyReason: Connect the midpoint formula with a supplied internal division ratio to establish a general coordinate result.

content.prompt:
$AE$, $BF$ and $CD$ are the medians of $\triangle ABC$. They are concurrent at the point $X$.

We also have:
$$\begin{aligned}BX&=2XF\\CX&=2XD\\AX&=2XE\end{aligned}$$
Show that $X$ has coordinates:
$$\left(\frac13(x_1+x_2+x_3),\;\frac13(y_1+y_2+y_3)\right).$$

spec.sourceRegion: Question 7, diagram to the right of the stem
spec.description: Triangle with three concurrent medians, labelled coordinate vertices and matching side-bisection ticks. Ordinary source blue strokes become black under house style; the origin label is omitted under the graph convention.
spec.mathematics: D, E and F are the midpoints of AB, BC and AC respectively. AE, BF and CD meet at X. Triple ticks identify AD=DB, single ticks identify BE=EC, and double ticks identify AF=FC. Drawing coordinates determine only the illustrative geometry and are not printed givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied geometry and labels remain visible in the question; no calculated coordinates are added.

answer.short:
$X=\left(\dfrac{x_1+x_2+x_3}{3},\dfrac{y_1+y_2+y_3}{3}\right)$.

Use the midpoint $F$ of $AC$ and $BX=2XF$, so $X$ lies two-thirds of the way from $B$ to $F$.
answer.worked:
Since $BF$ is a median, $F$ is the midpoint of $AC$:
$$F=\left(\frac{x_1+x_3}{2},\frac{y_1+y_3}{2}\right).$$
Since $BX=2XF$, $BF=3XF$, so $X$ lies two-thirds of the way from $B$ to $F$. Write $X=(x,y)$. Applying this fraction to the horizontal and vertical changes gives
$$\begin{align*}x&=x_2+\frac23\left(\frac{x_1+x_3}{2}-x_2\right)\\x&=x_2+\frac{x_1+x_3-2x_2}{3}\\x&=\frac{x_1+x_2+x_3}{3},\\y&=y_2+\frac23\left(\frac{y_1+y_3}{2}-y_2\right)\\y&=y_2+\frac{y_1+y_3-2y_2}{3}\\y&=\frac{y_1+y_2+y_3}{3}.\end{align*}$$
Therefore
$$X=\left(\frac13(x_1+x_2+x_3),\frac13(y_1+y_2+y_3)\right).$$
